meta.titre: System Software and Applications: what the operating system and utilities do for the user
meta.sous_theme: operating system, utility programs and types of application software

sections.contenu_markdown: A secretary in a school in Bamenda notices that the office computer opens files more and more slowly. A technician runs a maintenance tool, and a week later a payroll program written specially for the school is installed. Three different kinds of software appear in one story: the operating system that runs the machine, a utility that looks after it, and an application made for one customer. Examination questions ask you to describe each kind, to give a correct example, and to explain what the operating system does behind the scenes. Marks go to precise definitions and to examples that belong to the right family.

items: Hardware is the physical equipment of a computer; software is the set of programs that makes it work.
A program is a set of instructions that the processor executes.
Files are kept on backing storage such as a hard disk, and a program is loaded into RAM to run.

sections.titre: System software, utilities and application software
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Two families of software
| | System software | Application software |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | runs and maintains the computer and gives other programs a platform | carries out a task the user wants done |
| Examples | operating system, utility programs, device drivers, language translators | word processor, spreadsheet, payroll program, web browser |

### The operating system (OS)
The OS controls the hardware and decides how other programs use it. Its main roles are:
- **Process management**: scheduling the processor among the running programs so that each gets turns and several seem to run together.
- **Memory management**: giving each program its own area of RAM and stopping one program from overwriting another.
- **File management**: naming, storing, organising in folders, finding, copying and deleting files, and controlling who may open them.
- **Device management**: passing data to and from input, output and storage devices, with the help of device drivers.
- **Security and user interface**: user accounts, passwords and access rights, and the screen through which the user gives orders.

An interface is **command driven** when the user types text commands: the commands must be learnt, but the system needs little memory and an expert works quickly. It is **icon driven** (graphical) when the user points at windows, icons and menus: it is easy for a beginner, but it needs more memory and processing power.

### Utility software
A utility is a system program that carries out a maintenance task, for example antivirus, backup, file compression or disk formatting. A **disk defragmenter** is a utility. On a magnetic hard disk, saving, editing and deleting files leaves many files in scattered pieces. The defragmenter moves the pieces of each file next to each other and joins the free space, so the read head moves less and files open faster. It is not needed on a solid-state drive, which has no moving head.

Two other kinds of system software: a **device driver** lets the OS control one particular device such as a printer, and a **language translator** (assembler, compiler or interpreter) turns a program into a form the processor can execute.

### Application software and licences
- **General-purpose (off-the-shelf)** software is made for many users: it is cheap, tested and available at once, but it is not fitted exactly to one organisation.
- **Tailor-made (custom-written)** software is written for the exact needs of one organisation, for example a fee-collection program for one school. It fits well, but it costs more and takes time to develop.
- A **licence** is the permission to use software under stated conditions. A licensed (genuine) copy gives legal use, technical support, updates and a lower risk of hidden malware.

variantes.nom: Questions that say “describe ... and give an example”
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a kind of software must be described and illustrated.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write a one-sentence definition, then its purpose, then one named example of the right family. A utility is a program that maintains the computer, for example an antivirus or a disk defragmenter. Tailor-made software is written for the specific needs of one organisation, for example a records program written for one hospital. A word processor given as an example of a utility loses the example mark.

variantes.nom: Questions that say “explain TWO roles of the operating system”
variantes.quand_utiliser: When roles of the operating system are asked.
variantes.contenu_markdown: For each role write its name, what the OS does, and the result for the user. Memory management: the OS allocates a separate area of RAM to each program and protects it from the others, so several programs can stay open without overwriting one another. Give exactly the number of roles asked; a list of names without explanation earns very little.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When two types of system or software are compared.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Compare the two on the same point in each sentence: how the user gives instructions, how easy it is to learn, how much memory it needs. Two separate definitions with no contrasting point do not differentiate. For icon driven and command driven systems, contrast pointing at icons with typing commands, and the ease for beginners with the speed for experts.

sections.enonce_markdown: A pharmacy in Limbe has used the same computer for three years. (a) Distinguish between system software and application software, giving one example of each. (b) Explain how the operating system helps the pharmacist when a stock-control program and a word processor are open together. (c) Name a utility that can make the magnetic hard disk open files faster and explain how it works.

etapes.justification: Distinguish asks for a point of contrast, explain asks for how and why, and name and explain asks for a name followed by a reason.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (a) a contrast with examples, (b) how and why, (c) a name and a mechanism.

etapes.action: Answer (a) with a contrast and two examples.
etapes.justification: Two statements about purpose placed side by side show the difference, and each example must belong to the right family.
etapes.resultat_markdown: System software manages and maintains the computer, for example an operating system. Application software does a task the user wants done, for example a spreadsheet.

etapes.action: Answer (b) by linking the roles to the situation.
etapes.justification: Two programs are sharing the memory and the processor, which are the work of memory management and process management.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The OS gives each program its own area of RAM so that they do not overwrite each other, and it shares processor time between them so that both seem to run together.

etapes.action: Choose the utility in (c) from the symptom.
etapes.justification: Three years of saving, editing and deleting leave files in scattered pieces on a magnetic disk, and the symptom is slow opening.

etapes.action: Explain how it works and state the effect.
etapes.justification: The mark is for the mechanism and for its result.
etapes.resultat_markdown: It moves the pieces of each file next to each other, so the read head makes fewer movements and files open faster.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer**: (a) System software manages and maintains the computer and supports other programs, for example an operating system; application software performs a task wanted by the user, for example a spreadsheet. (b) Memory management gives each open program its own area of RAM and protects it from the other, and process management shares the processor between them so that both appear to run together. (c) A disk defragmenter moves the scattered pieces of each file next to each other, so the read head moves less and files open faster.

items.erreur_markdown: “A utility is application software because the user starts it.”
items.pourquoi_faux: A program is classed by its purpose. A utility maintains or protects the computer; it does not produce the documents, calculations or records the user needs.
items.correction_markdown: A utility is system software that carries out a maintenance task, such as antivirus, backup or defragmentation.

items.erreur_markdown: “Defragmentation deletes unwanted files to free space.”
items.pourquoi_faux: Defragmentation deletes nothing. It rearranges the pieces of files. Removing unwanted files is the job of a clean-up tool.
items.correction_markdown: Defragmentation stores the pieces of each file next to each other so the disk head moves less.

items.erreur_markdown: “A command driven system is controlled with icons and a mouse.”
items.pourquoi_faux: The two types are reversed. A command driven interface needs typed commands; the use of icons, windows and a pointer is the icon driven (graphical) interface.
items.correction_markdown: Command driven: typed commands. Icon driven: pointing at icons and menus.

items.erreur_markdown: “Tailor-made software is cheap because it is made for one person.”
items.pourquoi_faux: Software written for one organisation carries the whole cost of development and testing. It is usually more expensive than off-the-shelf software, which spreads its cost over many buyers.
items.correction_markdown: Tailor-made software fits the exact needs of the customer, but costs more and takes longer to obtain.

items.enonce_markdown: Name three utility programs and state in one sentence what each of them does.
items.solution_markdown: Award one mark for each correct utility with its task. Examples: antivirus (detects and removes malware); backup (copies files to another place so they can be restored); file compression (reduces the size of files to save space or speed up transfer); disk formatter (prepares a disk to receive files); disk defragmenter (stores the pieces of each file next to each other). **Any three correct utilities with correct tasks.**

items.enonce_markdown: A school bought one licensed copy of an accounting program. The bursar proposes to install it on four other office computers without buying more licences. (a) Give two reasons why the school should buy the extra licences. (b) Name the computer crime that the bursar's proposal would be.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Award one mark for each valid reason: use is legal; the school receives technical support and updates; genuine copies carry a lower risk of hidden malware; the developer is paid and keeps improving the product. (b) Using copies beyond the licence is **software piracy**.

items.enonce_markdown: A hospital must choose between an off-the-shelf patient-records package and a tailor-made one. (a) Describe tailor-made software and give an example. (b) Compare the two options on cost, fit to the hospital's needs and support. (c) Recommend one option and justify your choice.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Tailor-made software is written specially for the needs of one organisation, for example a records program written for that hospital. (b) Cost: off-the-shelf is cheaper because the cost is shared by many buyers, tailor-made is expensive to develop. Fit: off-the-shelf may lack needed features or contain unneeded ones, tailor-made does exactly what the hospital wants. Support: off-the-shelf support comes from the vendor and a large user community, tailor-made support depends on the developer. (c) Accept either choice if it is justified from the comparison, for example: **tailor-made, because the hospital has specific procedures that a general package would not match, and it can afford the development**; or **off-the-shelf, because it is cheaper, tested and available at once.** A recommendation with no reason earns no mark.

items_markdown: System software runs and maintains the computer; application software does the user's tasks.
The operating system manages processes, memory, files and devices, and provides security and the user interface.
Command driven means typed commands; icon driven means windows, icons, menus and a pointer.
A utility maintains the computer; a disk defragmenter stores the pieces of each file together so a magnetic disk reads faster.
Tailor-made software is written for one organisation: it fits well but costs more; off-the-shelf software is cheaper but general.
A licence gives legal use, support and updates; copying without one is software piracy.
